Guided demo

Click an edge, a list record, or a matrix 1 to light up all copies of that edge. Click a circle to focus a vertex.
⚠ Figure failed to load

plan.contextChunk: This figure sets three side-by-side panels, (a), (b), and (c), showing one small undirected graph and two ways of storing it. Panel (a) draws the graph as five gray circles numbered 1 through 5, with 1 at the upper left, 2 at the upper right, 3 at the far right, 4 at the lower middle, and 5 at the lower left, joined by seven straight edges: 1-2, 1-5, 2-5, 2-3, 2-4, 3-4, and 4-5. Panel (b) gives the adjacency-list form as a vertical array of five gray cells indexed 1 to 5, each holding a pointer arrow into a horizontal chain of two-field records whose right field is either an arrow onward or a diagonal slash marking the end. Row 1 chains 2 then 5; row 2 chains 1, 5, 3, 4; row 3 chains 2 then 4; row 4 chains 2, 5, 3; row 5 chains 4, 1, 2. Panel (c) gives the adjacency matrix as a bordered five-by-five grid of zeros and ones with rows and columns both headed 1 through 5, zeros along the diagonal and entries symmetric across it. Laying the picture beside the two tables lets a single edge be found three ways, and it makes plain that each undirected edge is stored twice.

interactionPlan.concept: One undirected graph can be stored either as adjacency lists or as an adjacency matrix, and in both representations every undirected edge {u,v} is recorded twice — once for u and once for v.
elements: Panel label (a) centered under the graph drawing
Panel label (b) centered under the adjacency-list structure
Panel label (c) centered under the adjacency matrix
Graph (a): five gray filled circles with black outlines labeled 1 (upper left), 2 (upper right), 3 (far right), 4 (lower middle), 5 (lower left)
Graph (a): seven straight black edges 1–2, 1–5, 2–5, 2–3, 2–4, 3–4, 4–5
Adjacency list (b): vertical array of five gray head cells stacked in a single column, row-labeled 1..5 to their left
Adjacency list (b): horizontal chain of two-field gray records to the right of each head cell; left field holds a vertex number, right field holds either a forward arrow or a diagonal slash (NIL)
Adjacency list (b): arrows from each head cell into its first record and between consecutive records
Adjacency list (b) contents: row 1 → 2, 5; row 2 → 1, 5, 3, 4; row 3 → 2, 4; row 4 → 2, 5, 3; row 5 → 4, 1, 2
Adjacency matrix (c): bordered 5×5 grid of 0/1 entries
Adjacency matrix (c): column headers 1..5 above the grid and row headers 1..5 to the left
Adjacency matrix (c): zeros on the main diagonal, entries symmetric across the diagonal
Highlight styling: selected edge drawn thick and colored, matching list records outlined, matching matrix cells shaded (same accent color)
Caption/annotation area showing the currently selected edge or vertex, e.g. 'edge {2,5} stored in list[2] and list[5]; cells (2,5) and (5,2)'

interactions.teaches: That a single undirected edge has exactly three simultaneous encodings — one line in the drawing, two list records, and two symmetric matrix cells — so storage of an edge is duplicated.

interactions.label: Focus vertex
interactions.teaches: That a vertex's neighbor set appears as edges at one node, as one linked chain, and as one row of the matrix — the same information in three shapes, with degree = chain length = row sum.

interactions.label: Endpoint u
interactions.teaches: Which vertex's list and matrix row will be touched by an edge update.

interactions.label: Endpoint v
interactions.teaches: That the second endpoint is not a passive partner — its list and matrix row must be edited too.

interactions.label: Add / remove edge {u,v}
interactions.teaches: That one edge change costs two record insertions/deletions in the list form but only two cell flips in the matrix form — the update cost difference between the representations.

demo_steps.title: One graph, three pictures
demo_steps.narration: The same five-vertex graph appears three ways: a drawing, five linked lists, and a 5×5 table of 0s and 1s. Nothing is highlighted yet — just notice that panel (b) has 14 records while panel (c) has 25 cells.

demo_steps.title: Follow one edge
demo_steps.narration: Click edge 2–5 in the drawing (or the 1 in cell (2,5)). The record '5' in list 2, the record '2' in list 5, and both cells (2,5) and (5,2) light up together: one edge, four stored copies of it in memory.

demo_steps.title: A vertex's neighbors, three ways
demo_steps.narration: Focus vertex 2. Its four incident edges glow in the drawing, its chain 1→5→3→4 lights up, and row 2 of the matrix shows four 1s. Degree, chain length, and row sum are the same number.

demo_steps.title: A sparse vertex
demo_steps.narration: Switch focus to vertex 3. Only two edges, a two-record chain, but still a full five-cell matrix row — the matrix pays for absent edges, the lists do not.

demo_steps.title: Add the missing edge {1,3}
demo_steps.narration: Set u = 1, v = 3 and press add. A new line appears in the drawing, a record is spliced into list 1 and into list 3, and cells (1,3) and (3,1) both flip from 0 to 1 — never just one of them.

demo_steps.title: Remove an existing edge {2,4}
demo_steps.narration: Set u = 2, v = 4 and press remove. Deleting from the lists means walking two chains to unlink two records; in the matrix it is two direct cell writes. Same edit, very different work.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: An undirected edge {u,v} is a single fact about the graph but is always stored twice — in list[u] and list[v], or in cells (u,v) and (v,u) — which is why |adjacency list records| = 2|E| and why the matrix is symmetric.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Three panels side by side on white, labeled (a), (b), (c) beneath. Left: the graph drawn with light-gray filled circles, thin black outlines, black numeric labels, and thin straight black edges; place 1 upper-left, 2 upper-right, 3 far right and slightly lower, 4 bottom center-right, 5 bottom left, so edges 1–2, 1–5, 2–5, 2–3, 2–4, 3–4, 4–5 stay uncluttered with 2–5 crossing the interior diagonally. Middle: a column of five light-gray head cells with small row labels 1–5 at the left, each head cell emitting a short arrow into a left-to-right chain of two-field gray rectangles; the left field carries the neighbor's number, the right field carries either an arrow to the next record or a diagonal slash for NIL. Chains: 1: 2,5 · 2: 1,5,3,4 · 3: 2,4 · 4: 2,5,3 · 5: 4,1,2. Right: a thin-bordered 5×5 grid with headers 1–5 above and to the left, 0/1 entries centered, zeros on the diagonal and perfect symmetry. Use one strong accent color (e.g. orange/red) for edge-lookup highlighting across all three panels, and a second, softer accent (e.g. blue) for the vertex-focus neighbor set, so the two highlight modes read distinctly. Newly added edges/records/cells should appear in green and removed ones should briefly show in gray strike-through before disappearing. Keep a one-line status caption under the panels naming the currently highlighted edge or vertex and its storage locations.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Click for edge lookup: click an edge in the graph or a 1 in the matrix, and the two adjacency-list entries plus the symmetric matrix cells highlight, showing how one undirected edge is stored twice.

authoredContext: The adjacency-list representation of a graph G D .V; E/ consists of an array Adj of jV j lists, one for each vertex in V . For each u 2 V , the adjacency list AdjŒu contains all the vertices _x0017_ such that there is an edge .u; _x0017_/ 2 E. That is, AdjŒu consists of all the vertices adjacent to u in G. (Alternatively, it may contain pointers to these vertices.) Since the adjacency lists represent the edges of a graph, in pseudocode we treat the array Adj as an attribute of the graph, just as we treat the edge set E. In pseudocode, therefore, we will see notation such as G:AdjŒu. Figure 22.1(b) is an adjacency-list representation of the undirected graph in Figure 22.1(a).

discrepancies: Default (step-0) state is not a clean drop-in replacement for the source: a dashed 'pending edge' line is drawn between vertices 1 and 3, dashed rings surround vertices 1 and 3, and a dashed outline sits on matrix cells (1,3)/(3,1) — none of this exists in the source figure and it clutters the first impression.

The whole drawing is scaled down inside a 1160×382 viewBox on a narrow container, so the text (matrix digits, list record numbers, the 0/1 cells) renders at roughly 7–10 px and is uncomfortably small compared with the large, bold numerals of the source.

The added explanatory caption line ('7 edges → 14 list records (2|E|) and a symmetric 5×5 matrix of 25 cells.') is an addition not present in the source and is rendered too small to read at inline size.

Panel (b) head column in the source is a single contiguous vertical array of five stacked cells sharing one long right border; the generated version uses five separate detached boxes, slightly weakening the 'array of list heads' reading.
Panel label placement: (a) sits at x≈170 which is off-centre relative to the graph drawing, and the whole figure leaves a large blank band below, making the composition less balanced than the source.
evaluation.notes: All three panels (graph, adjacency lists, adjacency matrix) are topologically and numerically faithful to the source with a rich, genuinely pedagogical set of interactions (step player, vertex focus, endpoint sliders, add/remove edge, cross-panel click highlighting), but the default state is polluted by dashed 'pending edge {1,3}' decorations absent from the source and all text renders too small to read comfortably at inline size.
action_items: Suppress the dashed pending-edge line, dashed vertex rings, and dashed matrix cell outline unless the user actually moves an endpoint slider, so step 0 matches the static source exactly.

Increase effective text size: shrink the viewBox (e.g. tighten to ~980×340 with less blank margin) and/or raise font sizes so matrix digits, record numbers, and (a)/(b)/(c) labels are legible at the rendered inline width.
Either drop the bottom caption from the default state or enlarge it and give it clear hierarchy (it currently reads as unreadable fine print below the figure).
Draw panel (b)'s list-head column as one contiguous 5-cell vertical array with a shared border, as in the source, and centre the '(a)' label under the graph drawing.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual decomposition and interaction set are correct; all action items are concrete rendering fixes (suppress default dashed decorations, enlarge text/tighten viewBox, caption hierarchy, contiguous head column, label centering).

discrepancies: The whole diagram is drawn into a 920×330 viewbox that scales down inside the container, so the numerals in the records, matrix cells and row/column headers render noticeably smaller than the large bold digits of the source, and a large blank band is left below the figure.

Panel (a) is drawn at a smaller scale relative to panels (b)/(c) than in the source (source vertices are large circles roughly the height of a list record plus margins); strokes on the graph edges are also thinner/lighter than the source's heavy black lines.

List record boxes are proportionally narrower and the inter-record arrows shorter than in the source, where the 'next' field and connecting arrow are visually longer and more prominent; head-column cells are also thinner relative to the record boxes.
Extra status caption text beneath the panels (appears on selection) and dashed 'pending edge' ghosting are additions not present in the source, though they stay out of the default state.
evaluation.notes: Faithful three-panel reproduction (graph, adjacency lists with correct orders and nil slashes, correct symmetric 0/1 matrix) with rich, genuinely pedagogical interactions (6-step demo, vertex focus, edge add/remove, cross-panel highlighting); the main weakness is that everything is rendered at a reduced scale so the numerals are smaller and lighter than the source's bold typography.
action_items: Tighten the viewbox (reduce vertical padding / unused width) or increase font sizes so the record and matrix digits render at roughly the source's visual weight at inline size.
Enlarge panel (a)'s vertices and thicken graph edge strokes so the graph drawing matches the visual weight and relative size it has in the source.
Widen the list record boxes and lengthen the next-pointer arrows slightly so panel (b) reads with the same proportions as the source linked-list diagram.
Ensure the status caption never overlaps the (a)/(b)/(c) panel labels at narrow viewports (clamp or move it into a dedicated strip).

feedback.rationale: Concept and plan are correct with no failure modes; remaining issues are purely implementation-level scaling, stroke weight, proportions, and caption placement fixes.

plan.concept: One undirected graph can be stored either as adjacency lists or as an adjacency matrix, and in both representations every undirected edge {u,v} is recorded twice — once for u and once for v.
elements: Panel label (a) centered under the graph drawing
Panel label (b) centered under the adjacency-list structure
Panel label (c) centered under the adjacency matrix
Graph (a): five gray filled circles with black outlines labeled 1 (upper left), 2 (upper right), 3 (far right), 4 (lower middle), 5 (lower left)
Graph (a): seven straight black edges 1–2, 1–5, 2–5, 2–3, 2–4, 3–4, 4–5
Adjacency list (b): vertical array of five gray head cells stacked in a single column, row-labeled 1..5 to their left
Adjacency list (b): horizontal chain of two-field gray records to the right of each head cell; left field holds a vertex number, right field holds either a forward arrow or a diagonal slash (NIL)
Adjacency list (b): arrows from each head cell into its first record and between consecutive records
Adjacency list (b) contents: row 1 → 2, 5; row 2 → 1, 5, 3, 4; row 3 → 2, 4; row 4 → 2, 5, 3; row 5 → 4, 1, 2
Adjacency matrix (c): bordered 5×5 grid of 0/1 entries
Adjacency matrix (c): column headers 1..5 above the grid and row headers 1..5 to the left
Adjacency matrix (c): zeros on the main diagonal, entries symmetric across the diagonal
Highlight styling: selected edge drawn thick and colored, matching list records outlined, matching matrix cells shaded (same accent color)
Caption/annotation area showing the currently selected edge or vertex, e.g. 'edge {2,5} stored in list[2] and list[5]; cells (2,5) and (5,2)'

interactions.teaches: That a single undirected edge has exactly three simultaneous encodings — one line in the drawing, two list records, and two symmetric matrix cells — so storage of an edge is duplicated.

interactions.label: Focus vertex
interactions.teaches: That a vertex's neighbor set appears as edges at one node, as one linked chain, and as one row of the matrix — the same information in three shapes, with degree = chain length = row sum.

interactions.label: Endpoint u
interactions.teaches: Which vertex's list and matrix row will be touched by an edge update.

interactions.label: Endpoint v
interactions.teaches: That the second endpoint is not a passive partner — its list and matrix row must be edited too.

interactions.label: Add / remove edge {u,v}
interactions.teaches: That one edge change costs two record insertions/deletions in the list form but only two cell flips in the matrix form — the update cost difference between the representations.

demo_steps.title: One graph, three pictures
demo_steps.narration: The same five-vertex graph appears three ways: a drawing, five linked lists, and a 5×5 table of 0s and 1s. Nothing is highlighted yet — just notice that panel (b) has 14 records while panel (c) has 25 cells.

demo_steps.title: Follow one edge
demo_steps.narration: Click edge 2–5 in the drawing (or the 1 in cell (2,5)). The record '5' in list 2, the record '2' in list 5, and both cells (2,5) and (5,2) light up together: one edge, four stored copies of it in memory.

demo_steps.title: A vertex's neighbors, three ways
demo_steps.narration: Focus vertex 2. Its four incident edges glow in the drawing, its chain 1→5→3→4 lights up, and row 2 of the matrix shows four 1s. Degree, chain length, and row sum are the same number.

demo_steps.title: A sparse vertex
demo_steps.narration: Switch focus to vertex 3. Only two edges, a two-record chain, but still a full five-cell matrix row — the matrix pays for absent edges, the lists do not.

demo_steps.title: Add the missing edge {1,3}
demo_steps.narration: Set u = 1, v = 3 and press add. A new line appears in the drawing, a record is spliced into list 1 and into list 3, and cells (1,3) and (3,1) both flip from 0 to 1 — never just one of them.

demo_steps.title: Remove an existing edge {2,4}
demo_steps.narration: Set u = 2, v = 4 and press remove. Deleting from the lists means walking two chains to unlink two records; in the matrix it is two direct cell writes. Same edit, very different work.

plan.keyInsight: An undirected edge {u,v} is a single fact about the graph but is always stored twice — in list[u] and list[v], or in cells (u,v) and (v,u) — which is why |adjacency list records| = 2|E| and why the matrix is symmetric.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Three panels side by side on white, labeled (a), (b), (c) beneath. Left: the graph drawn with light-gray filled circles, thin black outlines, black numeric labels, and thin straight black edges; place 1 upper-left, 2 upper-right, 3 far right and slightly lower, 4 bottom center-right, 5 bottom left, so edges 1–2, 1–5, 2–5, 2–3, 2–4, 3–4, 4–5 stay uncluttered with 2–5 crossing the interior diagonally. Middle: a column of five light-gray head cells with small row labels 1–5 at the left, each head cell emitting a short arrow into a left-to-right chain of two-field gray rectangles; the left field carries the neighbor's number, the right field carries either an arrow to the next record or a diagonal slash for NIL. Chains: 1: 2,5 · 2: 1,5,3,4 · 3: 2,4 · 4: 2,5,3 · 5: 4,1,2. Right: a thin-bordered 5×5 grid with headers 1–5 above and to the left, 0/1 entries centered, zeros on the diagonal and perfect symmetry. Use one strong accent color (e.g. orange/red) for edge-lookup highlighting across all three panels, and a second, softer accent (e.g. blue) for the vertex-focus neighbor set, so the two highlight modes read distinctly. Newly added edges/records/cells should appear in green and removed ones should briefly show in gray strike-through before disappearing. Keep a one-line status caption under the panels naming the currently highlighted edge or vertex and its storage locations.
